To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
cognitive loading affects motor awareness and movement kinematics but not locomotor trajectories in a virtual reality environment.
cognitive loading affects movement kinematics and motor awareness during goal-directed walking but not trajectory deviations.
cognitive load affected motor performance (i.e., kinematics and trajectory deviations), and motor awareness, but not trajectory formation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the central nervous system for the formation and control of goal-directed walking in virtual environments.
the effects of cognitive load on motor performance and awareness in goal-directed locomotion.
the question of how the brain controls movement.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cognitive load does not affect trajectory formation but does affect movement kinematics and the awareness of perturbed feedback.
cognitive load affects motor awareness, movement kinematics and motor planning but not motor execution and trajectory formation.
cognitive loading affects motor awareness, movement kinematics, but not the trajectory formation of goal-directed walking in virtual environments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cognitive load affects motor awareness and movement kinematics but not the formation of stereotypical walking trajectories.
cognitive load affects motor awareness but not motor performance in a VR environment.
cognitive loading does not affect the formation of locomotor trajectories but it does affect the movement kinematics and awareness of the perturbed visual feedback.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cognitive loading affects the kinematics of walking but not the trajectory formation in a VR environment, and that motor awareness is selectively impaired in conditions of high uncertainty.
the use of VR in rehabilitation settings should be carefully designed to avoid cognitive load and that the use of perceptually ambiguous feedback may impair motor awareness.
the VR environment we used is suitable for studying gait kinematics, trajectory formation and trajectory correction under cognitive load.
